decisions.note: Recorded contraction, not a free ratchet (#138). #121 removed the seven tools.expose* keys plus dev.hotReload, #136 replaced tests.enabled with the tower-tests row, and #133/#135 replaced docs.board/archive.enabled with the tower-board/tower-archive rows. The chain now continues here: the config-key surface is two-way like components, so any later increase or decrease needs its own dated decision.

#M39: one new key, review.mode (off/optional/required), replaces the deprecated review.requireReview boolean as the review policy. It is not a fifth component row: the reviewer preset row stays a capability, and the mode decides whether it is required (required) or unused (off). review.requireReview remains accepted for one release as a normalized alias, so it is a deprecated key rather than a removed one and the surface grows by exactly one.

#148/#149: the shape redesign adds the survey routing keys spawn.surveyPreset (core) and spawn.surveyModel (tuning), plus survey.sandbox (tuning) in the new survey section. tower-survey is the capability row; the preset/model names only route the read-only agent.

Review round 2 contracts the shape surface before release: spawn.surveyPreset could never be read (a survey's preset is shape-owned, so the key could only disagree with the registry) and survey.sandbox advertised a placement W1 does not implement. Only spawn.surveyModel remains as the optional model route; both removals are recorded here rather than silently shrinking the two-way surface.

#148 W2 implements the detached survey sandbox, so survey.sandbox returns as one tuning key: none (read-only shared checkout, the default and unchanged W1 behavior) or detached (a disposable detached worktree with a write/shell-capable preset). It is placement tuning, not a capability row or a second routing key; spawn.surveyPreset stays removed because the shape resolves the preset.

#148 W2 D5 adds gates.requireFreshSurvey (default false): the survey-stale dependency warning is advisory by default and becomes a merge blocker only when this gate is true. It is a merge-gate strictness key like the other gates.* entries, not a component.

#149 W4 contracts the surface by one: `tests.autoChecks` existed only to copy a discovery projection into the completion report, which made a second evidence shape. The receipt in mission.testRuns is now the one evidence shape read by domain/evidence.js, so the key has no remaining meaning and is removed rather than kept as a dead tuning switch.

#M66 (2.8.0): physically retires review.requireReview, the one-release alias accepted by #M39. review.mode is the only review policy key; the boolean is now rejected as config-unknown-key with a dated upgrade note naming the surviving key and the true -> required / false -> optional mapping, so the config surface contracts by one with no replacement key. See docs/guide/install-upgrade-migration.md.

#M76 (W5-B) bounds the append-only activity log: activity.maxBytes (default 4 MiB, 0 disables) and activity.retention (default 5) are tuning keys for adapter-enforced rotation. They are not a component row: rotation is always on by default and no capability disappears when it is tuned. The two keys are the only surface growth in this wave.

#162 adds one mode policy key, ralphPolicy (stop/refuse, default stop), mirroring planModePolicy for the Ralph stance: entering Tower mode with a live Ralph loop either stops and records it or refuses the entry. Tool denial stays #161's owner-derived default (no name is added to mode.denyTools); #162 adds only the command-owner surface and the loop sensor, so no tool, section or component moves.

#148/#149 restore the section count to its seed: survey.sandbox needs a home, so the survey section returns the 15 sections that #121 shrank to 14. Net zero against the seed; no other section changed.

Review round 2 removes the survey section with its only key: survey.sandbox advertised a detached read-only checkout W1 does not implement. The section existed only to hold that key, so the count returns to 14.

#148 W2 restores the survey section for its one tuning key, survey.sandbox (placement: none|detached). The section count returns to the 15 of the earlier shape cut; no other section changed and no component row was added (the sandbox preset is an internal child of the existing tower-survey group).

#M76 (W5-B) adds the activity section for its two tuning keys (activity.maxBytes, activity.retention). The section exists only to hold them; rotation is adapter behavior with no component row and no capability switch.

correction.reason: Measurement correction, not surface growth: the 2.3.0 baseline recorded only define()-registered tools. tower_mode and tower_control are registered directly by index.js, so the shipped surface was always 29 (#118). The recorder in host/tool-registry.js now covers both paths.

decisions.note: #163 Phase 3: the five read-only views (status/roster/diff/preflight/doctor) fold into tower_inspect, so 29 - 5 + 1 = 25 tools.
#163 Phase 4: init+adopt, finding+findings, mode+control and import_legacy+legacy_map each become one tool with an op/active field, so 25 - 4 = 21 tools.

The component surface joins the budget with its history. 2.0.4 shipped four top-level rows (tower, tower-skills, preset-tower-worker, preset-tower-reviewer); 2.3.0 replaced them with one tower-bundle group row that still mounts the same four sections. This is a recorded contraction, not a free ratchet: the seed stays at 4 so any further move -- including the #121 growth back to individually toggleable optional rows -- must extend this chain with a dated decision.

#121 restores the #65 policy from ADR 0005: the one tower-bundle group becomes a mandatory tower host anchor plus seven individually switchable optional rows (tower-skills, tower-batch, tower-import, tower-leases, tower-tests, tower-hmr shipped off, preset-tower-reviewer conditional). The host anchor and preset-tower-worker stay mandatory; tower_doctor and tower_recover stay mandatory with the host (#122), so they are not rows. configKeys and sections shrank in the same wave because the seven tools.expose* keys and dev.hotReload became rows.
#133: `docs.board` was a capability wearing a tuning-key costume. The visible tower-board row owns the MISSIONS.md board now; `docs.boardLocation` stays tuning. Off writes no board.
#135: `archive.enabled` was the same costume. The visible tower-archive row owns archival now; `afterDays`/`maxMissions` stay tuning. Off keeps terminal missions hot, so state keeps growing.

#134: the gate reads every shipped cordis.patch.yml, so the tower-ui row in ui-bundle/cordis.patch.yml joins the counted surface. The row was always shipped and unclassified; counting it is not new surface, it is the existing surface becoming visible to the policy.
#148/#149: tower-survey is a visible optional row: off means surveys cannot be planned and no survey agent is dispatched; build missions are unaffected.

#159: tower-artifact is a visible optional row for the third mission shape: off means artifact missions cannot be planned (tower_plan refuses kind:"artifact" with an actionable code) and no artifact mission exists to accept or merge; build and survey missions are unaffected. The row owns no tool and no preset — an artifact worker uses the mandatory worker preset — so it gates the shape, strictly better than all-off.
#163 Phase 3: one tower_inspect replaces five view schemas, so the profile loses those tools and their input bytes.
#163 Phase 4: init+adopt, finding+findings and mode+control collapse; tower_mode now also carries the write parameters.

#163 Phase 5: the tower profile no longer advertises tower_complete or tower_review; completing a mission and auditing a branch belong to the worker/survey and reviewer role presets. They stay in the default registered set (16) and the all-on build surface (21).

#163 Phase 1+2: the 26 repeated repoRoot fields leave the advertised schemas (the runtime resolves the repository) and 21 advertised alias fields become server-side only. A contraction, not a ratchet: any later per-profile increase still needs its own dated decision.
#163 Phase 3: one tower_inspect replaces five view schemas, so the profile loses those tools and their input bytes.
#163 Phase 4: three merges remove two schemas each but tower_mode now advertises read plus write plus the takeover authorization reference, so the net byte change is +26.
#163 Phase 5: the tower profile drops the tower_complete and tower_review input schemas with those two role-owned tools.

#159: the artifact shape adds two dimensions to two advertised schemas already in this profile — tower_plan's kind enum grows build|survey|artifact and gains artifacts[], and tower_mission gains accept plus accept_note. Both are optional properties inside existing schemas, so the tool count does not move; the schema text is the contract the worker briefing references.

#164: the role × phase gate lands on the #163 surface. Mode-off advertises tower_mode alone (1 tool, 846 B), idle adds tower_init (2/2,185), active is the default host-admitted union (14 tools, 14,977 B: the 16 mounted tools minus tower_complete/tower_review, which the #163 role predicate keeps on worker/survey and reviewer sessions); the worker/reviewer/survey presets advertise their #163 allow-lists (6/8,127, 5/6,000, 5/7,067 each).

Measurement correction (review R103), not a surface change: host:active was measured over the all-on build surface (21 tools / 22,061 B), which applies every optional capability row and counts the two role-owned tools no non-role host session admits. A session advertises the default host-admitted set instead — the 16 mounted tools minus tower_complete and tower_review — so host:active is 14 tools / 14,977 B. The 21-tool / 22,061 B figure stays documented as the build surface (tools.md) and is not a profile baseline.

#159: the artifact shape lands on the #163 surface. The plan/mission/complete input schemas grow to advertise the artifact deliverables and the human acceptance, so every profile that mounts those tools grows with them: host:active 14 tools / 16,017 B (was 14/14,977), preset:worker 6/8,646 (was 6/8,127), preset:survey and preset:survey-sandbox 5/7,586 each (were 5/7,067). The artifact worker reuses the mandatory worker preset, so no separate preset row appears. Mode-off, idle and reviewer are unchanged.
